businessModel: Search ads (non-personalised), Privacy Pro subscription (VPN, Identity Restoration), affiliate
updateCadence: Frequent app updates; web engine updates follow the OS/WebView2
summary: A lightweight privacy browser built on each OS's web engine: tracker blocking, Fire Button, Duck Player and YouTube ad blocking, Duck.ai on demand (one-click off). No extensions. No Linux version.
bestFor: Beginners wanting privacy with no setup
People who want a simple Duck.ai-integrated browser
notFor: People needing deep customisation or vertical tabs

pros.title: Simple and private by default
pros.detail: Tracker blocking, cookie pop-up handling and HTTPS upgrades work out of the box.

pros.title: Fire Button
pros.detail: One tap clears tabs and data.

pros.title: YouTube ad blocking
pros.detail: Duck Player and ad blocking on by default for most users (Q3 2026) on macOS, Windows, Android and iOS.

pros.title: AI with a kill switch
pros.detail: Duck.ai access with one-click "Use DuckDuckGo Without AI" on Windows and macOS.

pros.title: Encrypted sync
pros.detail: Sync & Backup syncs bookmarks and passwords end-to-end encrypted without email.

cons.title: No extensions
cons.detail: No extension support on any platform.

cons.title: Limited settings
cons.detail: Few tabs, appearance and advanced controls.

cons.title: No Linux build
cons.detail: No official Linux browser; DDG points to its extensions.

cons.title: Engine differences
cons.detail: Behaviour varies by OS engine; WebKit/WebView2 patch speed depends on the OS.

faq.q: Is there a DuckDuckGo browser for Linux?
faq.a: No official Linux browser as of Oct 2026; DDG offers extensions for Firefox/Chromium-based browsers instead.
No extensions on desktop or mobile.
